MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. Advertisement The success of the Moderna-Merck vaccine, intismeran autogene, may also usher in a new wave of treatments for other types of cancer, though experts are debating how broadly applicable the technology could be. The medicine is an individualized therapy that attacks the unique mutations, called neoantigens, found in a patient’s tumor. 10月28日，恒瑞医药发布2026年第三季度报告。第三季度，公司实现营业收入89.53亿元，同比增长20.55%；归母净利润24.58亿元，同比增长88.92%；利润总额27.76亿元，同比增长103.97%。前三季度，公司实现营业收入244.09亿元，归母净利润69.23亿元，同比增长20.38%。图源：恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告业绩增长的同时，恒瑞医药创新药业务也有新进展。CDE官网同日公示，公司自主研发的ADC药物瑞康曲妥珠单抗一项新适应症上市申请获受理。结合该药此前的临床研究及审评进展，此次申报可能涉及HER2阳性复发或转移性乳腺癌一线治疗，具体适应症仍需以官方披露为准。一、创新药销售超138亿元，对外授权持续贡献收入从前三季度经营情况来看，创新药已成为恒瑞医药收入的重要组成部分。2026年前三季度，公司创新药销售收入达138.71亿元，同比增长17.05%，占药品销售收入的比重提升至64.59%。其中，抗肿瘤创新产品收入98.65亿元，同比增长3.13%，占创新药销售收入的71.12%；非肿瘤创新产品收入40.06亿元，同比增长75.36%，占比达到28.88%。图源：整合于恒瑞医药2026年第三季度报告除产品销售外，创新药对外许可业务也为公司带来收入增量。前三季度，恒瑞医药创新药对外许可业务确认收入27.81亿元，同比增长31.12%，主要来自GSK、BMS相关合作的进度确认收入，以及个别已授权产品的里程碑款。同期，公司收到对外许可合作首付款及里程碑款现金共43.43亿元，主要包括BMS支付的6亿美元首付款。第三季度单季确认许可收入约13.6亿元，这类收入具有较高毛利率。在已授权项目持续贡献收入的同时，恒瑞医药也在拓展新的海外合作。2026年9月，公司与诺和诺德达成协议，将每周一次口服给药的GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂HRS-1596有偿许可给诺和诺德，授予其大中华地区以外全球范围内的开发、生产和商业化独家权利。该交易潜在总金额最高可达26亿美元，包括3亿美元首付款，以及后续开发、注册和商业化里程碑付款及销售提成。另一条出海路径是NewCo模式。8月6日，恒瑞医药的合作伙伴Braveheart Bio登陆美国纳斯达克。此前，恒瑞将自主研发的心肌肌球蛋白小分子抑制剂HRS-1893有偿许可给Braveheart Bio，并获得该公司部分股权。这是继今年4月Kailera Therapeutics登陆纳斯达克后，恒瑞医药NewCo模式取得的又一进展。二、多款创新药上市申请获受理，研发管线持续推进销售与授权业务之外，创新药研发及上市申报进展同样值得关注。2026年第三季度，恒瑞医药共有7项上市申请获CDE受理，其中GLP-1相关产品取得多项进展。企业公告+摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库整合具体来看，口服GLP-1受体激动剂HRS-7535片用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制、成人长期体重管理的两项上市申请均获受理；GLP-1/GIP双受体激动剂瑞普泊肽注射液用于成人2型糖尿病患者血糖控制的上市申请也获受理。从产品储备来看，截至目前，恒瑞医药已有27款1类创新药和6款2类新药在中国获批上市，另有100多个自主创新产品处于临床开发阶段，400余项临床试验在国内外开展。多款产品推进上市申报，也为公司后续创新药商业化提供了新的观察窗口。 Bristol Myers Squibb on Friday reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, a condition that causes muscle weakness and extreme fatigue, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. J.L. Kemny/Science Photo Library By Elaine ChenOct. 27, 2026 National Biotech Reporter Elaine Chen[email protected]Elaine’s stories explore the boom in new obesity treatments, new drug payment models, the ways companies are affected by FDA changes, and the emerging psychedelics drug sector. She co-writes The Readout newsletter, and co-hosts STAT’s weekly biotech podcast, The Readout Loud. You can reach Elaine on Signal at elaineywchen.70. Artiva Biotherapeutics said Tuesday that it’s winding down after two patients died in a trial testing its cell therapy for autoimmune diseases, the latest in a series of safety events that have emerged in a promising research field. One participant in the Phase 2 study died from a neurological complication after receiving the treatment, an NK cell therapy. Researchers determined the death was likely not related to the cell therapy itself, but to a chemotherapy that was given before the cell therapy, Artiva said. It’s standard to give patients chemotherapies before infusing cell therapies to lower the patients’ white blood cell count and make room for the new cells.Advertisement Related Story STAT Plus: Patient dies in Bristol Myers Squibb autoimmune CAR-T trial A second participant experienced sudden death about two months after treatment. Researchers determined that this was not related to any component of the treatment process, but the cause of death has not been determined, the San Diego-based company said. title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. title: 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 诺诚健华Q3营收大增150.60%：BD里程碑收入推高业绩，奥布替尼独挑商业化大梁 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 2026/10/29 3840 BTK 佐来曲替尼 坦昔妥单抗 奥布替尼 北京诺诚健华医药科技有限公司 药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华（688428.SH/09969.HK）第三季度营业收入同比大增150.60%。但同期药品销售收入增速为38.59%。两组数据出现明显剪刀差，内生盈利能力引发市场关注。10月26日，诺诚健华发布2026年第三季度报告显示，前三季度，公司实现营业收入20.99亿元，同比增长88.21%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润6.56亿元，扣除非经常性损益后的净利润为5.86亿元，实现持续盈利；经营活动产生的现金流量净额为2.20亿元，同比由负转正。图源：诺诚健华官网从增长动因看，除奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献外，诺诚健华与Zenas BioPharma（下称“Zenas”）的授权许可合作完成后续里程碑交付，成为营收增长的重要因素。另一方面，公司单品依赖问题仍较为突出。奥布替尼作为公司商业化收入的核心支柱，仍面临激烈竞争。在27日的业绩说明会上，以诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣为代表的部分高管，一方面坦承BD收入成为公司业绩核心助推力量；另一方面也表示，公司正在着手通过坦昔妥单抗、佐来曲替尼等产品强化公司的商业化盈利能力。一、BD里程碑收入助推单季净利扭亏诺诚健华成立于2015年，是一家处于商业化阶段的生物医药高科技公司，专注于恶性肿瘤及自身免疫性疾病领域一类新药的研发。公司于2020年3月在港交所上市，2022年9月登陆上交所科创板，并于2025年首次实现年度盈利。从单季度表现看，诺诚健华2026年第三季度实现营业收入9.62亿元，同比增长150.60%；归母净利润约4.09亿元，同比扭亏。公司在三季报中解释称，营收增长主要来自奥布替尼持续放量、坦昔妥单抗和佐来曲替尼新增销售贡献，以及与Zenas授权许可协议完成后续里程碑交付。不过，进一步拆分收入结构可以看到，公司整体营收增速明显快于药品销售增速。三季报显示，前三季度公司药品销售收入为14.49亿元，同比增长41.47%，而营业收入同比增长88.21%；单季度看，第三季度药品销售收入为5.31亿元，同比增长38.59%，而营业收入同比增长150.60%。药品销售增速与整体营收增速之间的明显差距，主要来自BD里程碑收入的确认。诺诚健华首席财务官傅欣在27日召开的业绩说明会上表示，扣除药品销售收入后的其余营业收入，主要是公司与Zenas达成的独家许可协议所实现的里程碑收入。回溯来看，2025年10月，诺诚健华子公司InnoCare US与Zenas签署授权协议，将奥布替尼、IL-17抑制剂和TYK2抑制剂在协议约定区域内的相关权益授予Zenas。2026年以来，相关交易对价陆续兑现：上半年公司已确认与IL-17抑制剂对外许可首付款相关收入；8月，InnoCare US又达成与奥布替尼相关的近期里程碑，有权获得Zenas 200万股普通股及2500万美元现金。在此背景下，BD收入对当期营收形成明显推升，而药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后独立支撑持续盈利，仍是市场关注的核心问题。前三季度研发、销售、管理费用分别为7.85亿元、4.23亿元、1.64亿元，三项费用合计约13.72亿元，规模和同期药品销售收入14.49亿元接近，这也意味着，在剔除BD收入后，诺诚健华内生商业化盈利压力不小。傅欣对此进一步表示，公司2026年第三季度实现持续盈利，2026年1—9月与上年同期相比扭亏为盈。但从目前收入结构来看，BD收入对公司业绩增长形成了较为明显的支撑，药品销售能否在覆盖相关费用后持续支撑盈利，仍待后续观察。二、奥布替尼贡献超九成商业化收入药品销售收入持续增长的背后，是诺诚健华对于奥布替尼这一核心产品的依赖。 2025年，诺诚健华商业化产品收入约14.42亿元，同比增长43.43%，其中，奥布替尼贡献收入14.10亿元，占比约97.78%。进入2026年，诺诚健华预计2026年全年药品销售收入增速有望超过35%，但目前公开资料未披露奥布替尼具体销售额。从药品销售收入来看，2026年前三季度，公司药品销售收入同比增长41.47%。在半年报中，诺诚健华将奥布替尼销售增长的驱动因素归结为一线适应症获批、医保覆盖扩大目标患者群体、差异化适应症定位，以及商业化团队持续提升市场渗透率等。不过，奥布替尼所在的BTK抑制剂市场竞争激烈。2025年医保目录调整后，包含奥布替尼在内已有五款BTK抑制剂纳入国家医保。诺诚健华在半年报中也表示，相关治疗领域已有多款获批产品及处于临床研究阶段的竞品，伊布替尼、泽布替尼等产品在中国的获批上市和纳入医保时间均早于奥布替尼，公司在市场推广方面面临一定竞争压力。对于BTK抑制剂国内目前的竞争格局，10月27日摩熵数科分析师向时代周报记者表示，据摩熵医药销售数据库，从医院端、实体药店及网上药店销售数据看，百济神州的泽布替尼2025年销售额达25.61亿元，2021—2025年年复合增长率为39.5%，占据较大市场份额；奥布替尼2025年销售额达10.02亿元，2021—2025年年复合增长率超过80.7%，放量速度较快，但市场份额仍需追赶。图源：摩熵医药-全终端销售数据库同时，上述分析师表示，随着国产BTK抑制剂陆续纳入医保，价格下降已经成为必然。行业竞争已经从市场抢占转向临床价值优势、医保支付覆盖、一线治疗获批等综合因素的竞争。这也意味着，尽管奥布替尼仍处于快速放量期，但诺诚健华对单一核心产品的依赖仍较为突出。目前，诺诚健华也正推动其他商业化产品逐步放量。公司执行董事、董事会主席兼行政总裁崔霁松在业绩发布会上表示，坦昔妥单抗于2026年迎来首个完整销售年度，预计将持续进行商业化贡献；佐来曲替尼为公司首款获批上市的实体瘤治疗药物，且儿科适应症的上市申请正在推进中，有望进一步覆盖更多患者人群。不过，与奥布替尼相比，上述产品目前收入贡献仍较为有限，能否随着商业化推进逐步放量，成为公司新的收入支柱，仍有待观察。 content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Gwendolyn Wu Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Corxel U.S. will go public via a merger with the SPAC Amanat Acquisition Corp., the companies announced Oct. 26, 2026. Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. Corxel's backers made clear in subsequent talks that they wanted the company to have a "more dedicated focus," rather than pursue "two different tracks," said Kevin Xie, its chief financial officer, in an interview with BioPharma Dive. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027. 2026/10/30 2696 Boehringer Ingelheim Fremont Inc 江苏先声医药科技有限公司 炎症性肠病 嘉兴安帝康生物科技有限公司 玛氘诺沙韦 10月28日，据国家药监局官网显示，嘉兴安帝康生物与先声药业合作开发的1类抗流感创新药玛氘诺沙韦片收到药品通知件，即未能获批上市。图源：NMPA官网玛氘诺沙韦是国内备受关注的抗流感创新药之一。该药最初由安帝康生物自主研发，2023年10月，先声药业与安帝康达成独家合作，获得其在中国地区流感适应症的独家商业化权益。此次上市申报未能顺利推进，也让这款曾被寄予期待的国产抗流感新药，再次成为行业关注的焦点。一、玛氘诺沙韦用药疗程短，单次口服1粒玛氘诺沙韦是一款具有全球自主知识产权的抗流感创新药，属于Cap依赖型核酸内切酶抑制剂。其通过抑制流感病毒Cap依赖型核酸内切酶活性，阻断病毒mRNA转录，从而抑制病毒复制。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在用药方式上，玛氘诺沙韦的一大特点是疗程短。相关资料显示，成人患者全程仅需单次口服1粒即可完成治疗。相较于需要多次给药的部分抗流感药物，这种给药方式有望提升用药便利性和患者依从性。摩熵医药数据库显示，玛氘诺沙韦于2021年首次申请临床，2025年3月首次申请上市，涉及甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒相关适应症。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从研发到商业化合作，再到上市申请，玛氘诺沙韦的进展也折射出国内抗流感创新药研发的持续推进。二、国产流感新药竞争持续升温玛氘诺沙韦的上市申报遇阻，也让国产抗流感药物的竞争格局再次受到关注。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，截至目前，国内已有10款流行性感冒新药获批上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2025年便密集迎来了太景生物科技的玛帕西沙韦、征祥医药的玛硒洛沙韦、广东众生药业的昂拉地韦、银杏树药业的玛舒拉沙韦4款国产新药的密集获批上市，让国产抗流感药物正全面驶入爆发期。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月13日，上海爱科百发生物医药技术股份有限公司宣布，其自主研发的首款抗流感Fc偶联物（AFC）新药AK0406注射液，用于流感预防适应症的临床试验申请正式获得国家药监局批准。这是中国首个进入临床阶段的流感AFC药物，填补了国内长效抗病毒流感预防领域的技术空白。三、结语随着更多创新药和改良型新药陆续推进，流感治疗领域的竞争正逐渐延伸至作用机制、给药方式及临床应用场景等多个维度。对玛氘诺沙韦而言，后续审评进展及商业化前景仍值得关注。参考来源：[1] 摩熵咨询 仿制药 行业政策法规 创新药/改良型新药 26页 免费下载 1.4.1 本周全球TOP10创新药研发进展（1）GSK乙肝治愈药物Hibsago获 FDA 批准上市10月20日，GSK宣布，其下反义寡核苷酸（ASO）创新药 Hibsago（bepirovirsen，贝普若韦生）已获得美国FDA正式批准上市，与核苷（酸）类似物逆转录酶抑制剂（NrtI）联合用于治疗慢性乙型肝炎（CHB）病毒感染。今年8月，Hibsago在日本首次获批，成为日本首个获批用于实现慢性乙肝功能性治愈的治疗方案。Bepirovirsen最初由Ionis Pharmaceuticals发现。2019年，GSK从Ionis获得了该药物的全球开发和商业化权利。本次获批基于B-Well 3期临床项目的积极结果，该项目包括B-Well 1和B-Well 2两项研究。此前发布的汇总数据显示，在基线HBsAg水平≤3000 IU/mL的成人患者中，bepirovirsen联合标准治疗实现了19%的功能性治愈应答率，而安慰剂联合标准治疗组的这一比例为0%。FDA曾授予bepirovirsen突破性疗法认定。（2）诺华在研放射性配体疗法拟纳入突破性治疗品种10月21日，CDE官网显示，诺华（Novartis）申报的[225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617注射液拟纳入突破性治疗品种，拟用于治疗接受过雄激素受体通路抑制剂（ARPI）和紫杉类化疗且在[177Lu]Lu-PSMA靶向治疗期间或治疗后出现进展的前列腺特异性膜抗原（PSMA）阳性转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）成人患者。公开资料显示，225Ac-PSMA-617是一种在研的基于锕同位素的放射配体疗法（RLT），利用已验证的配体靶向PSMA，将短射程、高能量的α粒子辐射直接递送至前列腺癌细胞，诱导肿瘤细胞DNA链断裂实现肿瘤细胞杀伤，同时尽可能减少周围健康组织暴露。（3）进口肝病新药依非兰诺片在中国申报上市10月21日，CDE官网显示，益普生按注册分类5.1类申报的依非兰诺片国内上市申请获受理。早前，8月19日，该药已纳入优先审评，拟定适应症为：与熊去氧胆酸（UDCA）联合治疗对UDCA应答不足的成年患者的原发性胆汁性胆管炎（PBC），或在无法耐受UDCA的患者中用作单药治疗。据公开资料显示，依非兰诺（Elafibranor片）是一款新型的口服PPARα/δ双重激动剂，每日一次。2024年6月，依非兰诺率先在美国获批，成为近十年来首个获批用于治疗罕见肝病PBC的新药。该批准主要基于III期ELATIVE研究数据。与安慰剂联合UDCA组（n=53）相比，依非兰诺联合UDCA组（n=108）达到生化应答复合主要终点的患者比例高出13倍（分别为51%和4%，治疗差异达47%）。（4）伦康依隆妥单抗第四个适应症上市申请获CDE受理10月21日，CDE官网显示，百利天恒自主研发的全球首创(First-in-class)、新概念(New concept)、目前全球首个且唯一获批上市的双抗ADC 伦康依隆妥单抗（宜泽康®，BL-B01D1/iza-bren），治疗既往接受过内分泌治疗且在晚期疾病阶段接受过至少一线化疗的不可切除或转移性的HR+HER2-乳腺癌的药品上市申请（NDA）已获得正式受理。这是伦康依隆妥单抗继鼻咽癌、食管鳞癌、三阴性乳腺癌后，获CDE受理的第四项上市申请。本次新增适应症的上市申请，是基于伦康依隆妥单抗在HR+HER2-乳腺癌的Ⅲ期临床试验（研究方案编号：BL-B01D1-306）的期中分析结果。2026年8月，经独立数据监查委员会（iDMC）判断，该研究在预设的期中分析中达到无进展生存期（PFS）主要终点，成为伦康依隆妥单抗第5个达到主要终点的Ⅲ期临床研究，也是全球首个双抗ADC药物在HR+HER2-乳腺癌治疗中达到主要终点的Ⅲ期临床研究。（5）阿斯利康/第一三共重磅ADC新适应症在中国获批上市10月22日，阿斯利康宣布，其与第一三共共同开发与商业化的 优赫得®（英文商品名：Enhertu®，通用名：注射用德曲妥珠单抗）于2026年10月20日正式获得中国国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）批准，单药适用于治疗既往接受过治疗或无满意替代治疗方案的不可切除或转移性HER2表达为IHC 3+的成人实体瘤患者。该适应症是基于单臂临床试验的结果给予的附条件批准。该适应症的完全批准将取决于开展的确证性试验的临床获益。本次获批是基于四项II期试验结果，其中包括三项全球研究：DESTINY-PanTumor02、DESTINY-Lung01、DESTINY-CRC02和一项中国研究DESTINY-PanTumor03，研究结果表明德曲妥珠单抗在多种实体瘤类型中均展现出具有临床意义的应答。值得一提的是，这是德曲妥珠单抗在中国获批的第十项适应症，也是国内首个获批泛肿瘤适应症的HER2靶向ADC。（6）强生双抗新药特立妥单抗在中国获批新适应症10月22日，强生宣布，其申报的特立妥单抗通过优先审评审批程序在国内获批一项新适应症，适用于既往至少接受过一线治疗的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤成人患者。特立妥单抗是一款可同时靶向BCMA和CD3的双抗。2022年8月，特立妥单抗率先在欧盟获得附条件批准，成为全球首款获批上市的BCMA×CD3双抗，随后该药又陆续在美国、中国和日本等市场获批。该药最初主要用于接受过多线治疗的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤患者，近年来则不断向更早治疗线次及联合用药拓展。2026年3月，美国FDA批准特立妥单抗的一项新适应症，联合达雷妥尤单抗皮下注射用于多发性骨髓瘤治疗。在中国，特立妥单抗于2024年8月首次获批上市，单药适用于既往至少接受过三线治疗（包括一种蛋白酶体抑制剂、一种免疫调节剂和一种抗CD38单克隆抗体）的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤成人患者。本次是该药在中国获批的第2项适应症。此次批准主要基于MajesTEC-9研究的积极结果。（7）瑞博生物在研1类siRNA新药RBD4059注射液获批临床10月22日，CDE官网显示，瑞博生物申报的1类新药 RBD4059注射液（vortosiran）获批临床，拟开发用于心房颤动患者的卒中预防。RBD4059是由瑞博生物精心研发的核心产品管线之一，是全球首款靶向凝血因子XI（FXI）的抗血栓siRNA候选药物。FXI作为内源凝血途径的关键分子，其在血液凝固过程中发挥着至关重要的作用。RBD4059通过特异性地靶向FXI的信使核糖核酸（mRNA），精准地抑制其蛋白表达和活性，从而有效地阻断内源性凝血途径的激活，达到抗凝血、抗血栓的效果。研究表明，FXI水平天然偏低的人群罹患血栓性疾病概率较低，且不会增加自发性出血风险。因此，FXI抑制已成为当前极具前景的潜在治疗手段，既能有效预防血栓形成，同时相较于现有抗凝疗法具有更高的安全性。（8）康方生物依沃西单抗又一适应症拟纳入优先审评10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物依沃西单抗注射液的一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗用于局部晚期或转移性胆道癌的一线治疗。此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。依沃西是康方生物自主研发的、全球首创PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。在中国，依沃西已经获批三项适应症，适应症包括EGFR-TKI耐药的nsq-NSCLC、一线治疗PD-L1阳性NSCLC、一线治疗鳞状NSCLC。（9）石药集团/和铂医药新药巴托利单抗获批上市10月23日，石药集团与和铂医药宣布，中国国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）已批准 恩力达®（巴托利单抗注射液，皮下给药，170 mg (1 mL)/瓶；商标持有人：石药集团）上市，用于治疗抗乙酰胆碱受体（AChR）抗体阳性的成人全身型重症肌无力（gMG）患者。此次获批基于一项在中国27家研究中心开展的关键性3期临床研究的积极结果。巴托利单抗是一款靶向新生儿Fc受体（FcRn）的全人源单克隆抗体，通过阻断FcRn介导的免疫球蛋白G（IgG）抗体再循环，加速致病性IgG自身抗体的降解，为包括gMG在内的自身免疫性疾病提供了一种靶向治疗方法。巴托利单抗最初由HanAll 用于中重度特应性皮炎的 Ⅱ 期临床试验已顺利完成，成功达成主要研究终点，安全性与耐受性表现良好。目前项目已进入 Ⅲ 期关键性注册临床阶段。该项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照研究由北京大学人民医院牵头，已入组 461 例受试者，主要终点为第 16 周EASI-75 应答率与 IGA 应答率。1.4.2 emvistegrast，或接受安慰剂治疗。在200 mg高剂量组的59例患者中，第12周有33例达到临床应答，比例为66%；安慰剂组60例患者中有22例达到临床应答，比例为37%（名义P值＜0.001）。其他疗效指标方面，200 mg content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a Roche lung cancer drug, a Bristol CAR-T trial death, and more Most recently approved cancer drugs in Europe do not offer high clinical benefit, analysis finds Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanOct. 26, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to another working week. We hope the weekend respite was relaxing and invigorating because that oh-too-familiar routine of meetings, deadlines, and the like has returned with a vengeance. But what can you do? The world, such as it is, continues to rotate. To nudge it in a better direction, we are brewing another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is butter pecan with a dash of raw honey. Feel free to join us. Remember, no prescription is required. Meanwhile, here are some tidbits to help you along. Best of luck accomplishing your goals today, and of course, do keep in touch. … Bristol Myers Squibb reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research, STAT notes. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release. In a subsequent statement, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”Advertisement A Roche drug billed as a potential blockbuster helped patients with a form of lung cancer that had spread live almost six months longer than two competitive medicines, Bloomberg News says. The experimental treatment, called divarasib, fared better than similar drugs from Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb in a late-stage study. The drug was given to patients with non-small cell lung cancer that had spread, in part because of a genetic mutation, after other treatments, including chemotherapy. The findings could help divarasib become the treatment of choice for this type of lung cancer, in which a mutation called KRAS G12C drives the tumor cell growth. title: FDA Approves Ilumya for Adults With Active Psoriatic Arthritis
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 30, 2026 FDA Approves Ilumya for Adults With Active Psoriatic Arthritis Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Sun Pharma's IL-23 inhibitor tildrakizumab gains a psoriatic arthritis indication; the announcement cited no phase 3 efficacy figures. Advertisement FDA has approved Sun Pharma’s Ilumya (tildrakizumab-asmn) for adults with active psoriatic arthritis, the company announced Oct. 30.1 The decision adds a second disease to the label of the interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor, which FDA first approved in 2018 for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The expansion extends the product from dermatology into rheumatology, where Sun Pharma estimates that as many as 2.4 million Americans live with the disease.1“FDA approval of Ilumya for adults with active psoriatic arthritis represents another important innovative medicine milestone for Sun Pharma and builds on the established clinical experience of Ilumya in plaque psoriasis,” said Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, Sun Pharma. “As an IL-23 inhibitor administered exclusively by a healthcare provider, Ilumya is now an option for adults with active psoriatic arthritis who are unable to self-administer treatment or who may benefit from regular in-office care.”1Key FactsDrug: Ilumya (tildrakizumab-asmn), IL-23 inhibitorIndication: Adults with active psoriatic arthritisTrials: Phase 3 INSPIRE-1 and INSPIRE-2Efficacy: ACR20 endpoint met at week 24 (no rates)Safety: No new signals reported by companyStatus: FDA-approved; U.S.; clinician-administeredSun Pharma is positioning provider administration as the product’s distinguishing feature. The announcement did not address launch timing, pricing or how payers might view an in-office model. Ilumya is also approved for plaque psoriasis in India, Australia, Canada, China and Japan, and in Europe as Ilumetri, which Almirall markets.1What data support the approval?The approval rests on two phase 3 studies, INSPIRE-1 and INSPIRE-2, which compared Ilumya 100 mg with placebo over 52 weeks in adults with active psoriatic arthritis.1 INSPIRE-1 enrolled patients with prior exposure to a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitor and INSPIRE-2 enrolled patients without it; together they included more than 800 participants. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 20% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR20) at week 24, and the company reported in 2025 that both studies met it.2 The announcement did not include ACR20 response rates. Sun Pharma said the studies identified no new safety signals and that safety was consistent with the drug’s established profile. Upper respiratory tract infections were among the most common adverse reactions in the arthritis studies, and patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis before treatment begins.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); How does it fit the psoriatic arthritis treatment landscape?Psoriatic arthritis can cause joint pain, swelling and stiffness that may lead to permanent joint damage, and roughly one in three people with psoriasis also have it, according to the company. Sun Pharma adds that more than 15% of people with psoriasis may have undiagnosed psoriatic arthritis.1 Treatment options already include biologic drugs that target TNF and targeted synthetic agents.3“Psoriatic arthritis is a complex and chronic disease. As clinicians, we need a range of therapeutic options that allow us to individualize care based on each patient’s symptoms and treatment goals. Adding an IL-23 inhibitor option that is administered by a healthcare provider gives us a new way to offer appropriate patients additional support and engagement with their healthcare team,” said Philip Mease, Director of Rheumatology Research at the Swedish Medical Center and Providence St Joseph Health and Clinical Professor at the University of Washington School of Medicine, Seattle, WA.1 Mease was first author of the earlier phase 2b study of tildrakizumab in the condition.3What did earlier studies show?Ilumya’s psoriasis record is longer than its arthritis record. In the phase 3 reSURFACE 1 and 2 trials, 61% to 66% of patients receiving 100 mg or 200 mg achieved a 75% improvement in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index at week 12, compared with 6% on placebo.4 In a phase 2b study of 391 patients with active psoriatic arthritis, 71.4% to 79.5% of those receiving Ilumya reached ACR20 at week 24, versus 50.6% on placebo. A higher-than-expected placebo response made results harder to interpret, and improvement in dactylitis and enthesitis was not observed.3What questions remain unanswered?Sun Pharma said in 2025 that full phase 3 findings would be presented at a future medical meeting and published.2 The Oct. 30 announcement included no effect sizes, secondary endpoints or results by prior TNF exposure.1Efficacy was assessed after two doses at 24 weeks, but the announcement did not describe how durable responses were beyond that point.1 Whether the high placebo response seen in the phase 2b study recurred in the phase 3 studies cannot be assessed without the data.SourcesILUMYA (tildrakizumab-asmn) approved in the U.S. for the treatment of adults with active psoriatic arthritis. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. This is the second major PRO-XTEN collaboration — an earlier $1.7 billion deal with Astellas for a PSMA-targeted TCE in prostate cancer was announced in February 2026. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline.
